title: Top 10 Women's College Basketball Players to Collect in 2026
meta_description: JuJu Watkins, Sarah Strong and eight more college stars ranked for card collectors, with specific cards, card images, research links and risks to watch.
summary: Ryan's editorial ranking of ten college players. The page is a straight list: title, lead SuperFractor, two intro sentences, then items 1 through 10. Each section photo is the highest completed sale found for that player, with one price line. His paragraphs still discuss the cards he studied.

uniqueness.summary: Each section photo is a verified high sale, with the price, date and source on one line under the image.
points: Goldin totals include the 22% buyer's premium: Watkins $24,404 on a $20,003 bid, Strong $1,220 on a $1,000 bid
Fanatics Collect totals with buyer's premium: Hidalgo aqua autograph PSA 10 at $150, Crooks gold patch autograph CGC AUTH at $28.80
Single-price SportsCardsPro sales only. Two-price Booker gold shimmer rows and guide prices were not used

unique: Each section photo is the highest completed sale found for that player, with one price line under the image
Goldin buyer totals: Watkins 1/1 SuperFractor PSA 10 at $24,404 and Strong 1/1 patch SuperFractor PSA 7 at $1,220
SportsCardsPro single-price sales for Booker, Blakes, Edwards, Fulwiley, Williams and Cambridge. Two-price rows were skipped
unverified: No completed JuJu Watkins sale near $40,000 was found. The article does not claim one. The lead and her section photo are the Goldin 1/1 SuperFractor at $24,404.
Sports Card Investor pages for a Crooks black-and-gold stealth autograph and a Booker gold refractor returned a captcha or no dated rows, so those higher claims were not used.
Booker's gold shimmer SportsCardsPro rows show two prices each and were skipped. The gold refractor page had no completed sales.
Fulwiley's gold wave catalog photo on SportsCardsPro is only 135 by 179 pixels. The $170 sale row on that page is a single price.
PSA cert lookup pages were not re-opened. Cert numbers 123955080 and 162277779 come from the Goldin lot pages.
The Topps Edwards page and the Topps Blakes print run were not re-opened. Ryan's paragraphs still cite them.

categories.name: Accuracy
categories.reason: Each new price was read from a page that loaded: Goldin sold totals for Watkins and Strong, Fanatics Collect sold totals for Hidalgo and Crooks, and single-price SportsCardsPro rows for the other six. Two-price rows, guide prices, and captcha-blocked Sports Card Investor claims are not in the article. No sale near $40,000 is claimed.

categories.name: Information gain
categories.reason: Each photo is now a higher verified sale than the base card Ryan discusses, with the price and date on one line. The ranking board and buying checklist are still gone, so the page does not also work as a shopping list.

categories.name: Effort and replication cost
categories.reason: Goldin lot pages, Fanatics Collect sold lots, and SportsCardsPro sale tables were opened for all ten players. Buyer premiums were checked against the stated 22 percent on the two Goldin lots.

categories.name: Originality
categories.reason: The ranking and the cards he discusses are still his. The photos are a separate verified sale for each player, including the 1/1 patch SuperFractor for Strong and the red autographs for Edwards and Cambridge.

categories.name: Experience and expertise
categories.reason: The first-person judgments in the ten sections are Ryan's. The intro is two of his sentences. The added collection sentence was trimmed with the rest of the intro.

categories.name: Main content and layout
categories.reason: The title is above the fold on desktop and phone. The lead SuperFractor sits under the byline, two intro sentences follow, and item 1 is next. Each section is a heading, a card, one price line, and his text. After item 10 there is only the short bottom line and fine print.

categories.name: Transparency
categories.reason: The lead caption and the research note separate winning bids from buyer totals. Each section line names the price, the grade when the sold copy was graded, the date, and Goldin, Fanatics Collect, or SportsCardsPro. The how-made note says Ryan wrote the article.

categories.name: Writing craft
categories.reason: Ryan's section order is intact. The repeated risk label is different on each player, and the closing tells a reader to follow players and learn the cards.

categories.name: People-first purpose
categories.reason: A collector sees the expensive sold card under each name, with the price and the source on the next line, and can ignore guide prices and two-price rows that were left out.

categories.name: Human voice
categories.reason: The body is Ryan's wording, with light edits on the flagged contrast lines. The ranking and the I/my judgments are his.

scorecard.info_gain: The photo under each player is the highest completed sale found, with the price, date and source on one line, kept separate from the cheaper card Ryan still discusses.
ai_flags: The flagged contrast lines were rewritten in plain sentences. Ranking, structure, and the rest of the wording are Ryan's.
Fact-check and formatting edits cite the Watkins $42.01 sale to SportsCardsPro and rename Fulwiley's award to SEC Sixth Woman of the Year.
Ryan should still read the edited lines before the article is published.
Card photos were moved under the byline and under each section heading. The wording was left for Ryan to edit.
No sale near $40,000 was verified. The lead uses the Goldin 1/1 SuperFractor at a $20,003 winning bid and a $24,404 total. Purple Lava stays in section 1.
The sold-price table was replaced with a one-line sale under each section photo and a thumbnail grid before the bottom line. Method notes moved to the research note.
List structure now runs title, lead image, two intro sentences, items 1 through 10, then the bottom line and fine print. The quick board, five checks, and sales grid were removed.
Section photos were swapped to the highest verified completed sale for each player. Ryan's paragraphs still name the cards he studied.
